2026-11-16 — forwarding: 47 bare -> 44 (-3), total 1302 -> 1299.

The first tenant context this module has ever had: `forwarding` was 0 of 47
operations contextualised, so under Phase 2 (app.rls_strict = on) RLS
protected nothing in it.

The three operations that came inside `withTenant` are the ones that carry
regulatory weight — the shipment-file milestone advance and the two customs
declaration lifecycle writes (submit, setStatus). The remaining 44 are reads
and creates that already carried an explicit `companyId` filter.

Re-recorded to bank the improvement. Under the per-module ratchet, leaving the
baseline at 47 would let forwarding drift back to 47 bare without failing.

2026-11-16 — process-control: 60 bare -> 52 (-8), total 1310 -> 1302.

`src/process-control` was the largest module in the codebase with no tenant
context at all: 60 tenant operations, zero of them inside `withTenant`. Under
Phase 2 (app.rls_strict = on) that means RLS protects nothing in this module —
isolation rested entirely on each query remembering to add `companyId`.

The four lifecycle writes in `completeStep`, `raiseIncident`, `resolveIncident`
and `recordOutcome` now run inside `withTenant`, and every status transition
is a compare-and-set `updateMany` scoped on `{ id, companyId, status }`.

The eight operations that came inside are the ones that matter most: they are
the writes that move a process between states. The remaining 52 are reads and
creates that already carried an explicit `companyId` filter.

Re-recorded to bank the improvement. Under the per-module ratchet, leaving the
baseline at 60 would have let process-control drift back to 60 bare without
failing — an improvement only holds if it is recorded.

2026-11-16: route load and scan moved out of the controller into
src/manifests/load-scan.service.ts, and its queries run inside withTenant().
Total 1314 -> 1310: a net fall of four, because the six operations the
controller used to perform bare are now contextualised and only the GET
remains in the controller. Contextualised rose to 205.

The wrapping is a correctness change here, not only a coverage one. The old
verifyScan read the manifest, then the waybill, then wrote IN_TRANSIT as
three separate round trips, so a dispatch landing between the first read and
the write would load a parcel onto a vehicle that had already left. Making
the decision inside one tenant transaction closes that window, and the
status write itself is compare-and-set.

This is also the first change to add a column for load control:
manifest_waybills.scannedAt, migration 20261116090000. Without it a re-scan
and a parcel already on another truck are indistinguishable, since both
present as waybill status IN_TRANSIT.


2026-11-13: client profitability and the dashboard summary now cost from
recorded data too (src/commercial-analytics/client-profitability.service.ts).
Total 1315 -> 1314: the invoice and period-total queries run inside
withTenant(), joining invoice -> invoice item -> waybill ->
DeliveryCostAllocation, so they moved from bare to contextualised.
Contextualised rose to 188.

This closes the customer axis of the same defect as the lane fix, and it is the
one that mattered more. The matrix used to charge every client
deliveryCount x flatRate and then issue a PROFITABLE / MARGINAL / UNPROFITABLE
verdict, so two customers billed identically earned the same label no matter
what they cost to serve. The dashboard summary issued HEALTHY / WARNING /
CRITICAL the same way. Both now refuse a verdict when the cost is modelled:
health is UNKNOWN and marginHealth is UNKNOWN, because telling an operator a
customer is unprofitable is a commercial decision that must not be made from an
average. Where cost IS recorded the verdict can differ from the flat-rate one,
and the tests pin that it does.

2026-11-13: lane profitability now reads recorded cost instead of charging
every delivery the same modelled rate
(src/commercial-analytics/lane-profitability.service.ts). Total 1316 -> 1315:
the two queries behind it — DeliveryCostAllocation and Waybill — run inside
withTenant(), so they moved from bare to contextualised rather than adding to
the unprotected backlog. Contextualised rose to 184.

This is a correctness change, not just a coverage one. The endpoint used to
cost every lane as deliveryCount x (fuelCostPerKm x avgKmPerDelivery +
driverHourlyCost x avgMinutes/60 + vehicleCostPerKm x avgKmPerDelivery +
overheadPerDelivery): a flat rate per stop, identical for a 5 km urban drop and
a 900 km cross-border haul, with no tolls and none of the fuel actually bought.
It was returned as profitability, including a PROFITABLE / MARGINAL /
UNPROFITABLE verdict per client derived from it. The Trip Truth engine had
already written the real per-waybill cost to DeliveryCostAllocation, stamped
MEASURED or ALLOCATED, and the dashboard was not reading it.
2026-11-13: booking portal added (src/booking-portal/). Total 1315 -> 1316, and
the module contributes exactly one of that. Of the 15 tenant operations it
performs, 14 are contextualised: every tenant-surface read and write, and the
anonymous write, run inside withTenant(), so row-level security backs the WHERE
clause instead of relying on it alone.

The one bare operation is the link lookup by token in
booking-portal-link.resolver.ts. It cannot be scoped: the company is the answer
that lookup returns, not an input it can filter on — the same position
auth.service.ts is in when it resolves a user by email before login. It is
deliberately isolated in its own file, because the coverage scanner exempts per
file and a shared file would have exempted the 14 scoped operations alongside
it. The write that follows runs under withTenant(link.companyId), so the public
path is scoped from the first moment a tenant exists rather than being the one
surface RLS never covers.

Two notes for whoever reads this next. The ownership check inside updateLink and
revokeLink is inlined rather than factored into a helper: the scanner classifies
by lexical position inside the withTenant() call and cannot see through a method
call, so the factored version was reported as an unprotected read while being
protected. And booking_requests had no tenant column at all until migration
20261115090000 in this change — it shipped carrying only linkId, so the RLS
sweep of 20261012210000 could not cover it and any lookup by id would have
resolved for every company.

Bare tenant operations per module, at the time this was recorded. The invariant enforced by --check is that the TOTAL may never rise. Re-record only when coverage has genuinely improved, and say how in the commit.
2026-11-12: journey.service.ts moved from driver-portal/ to journeys/; its 23 bare
operations moved with it (driver-portal 66 -> 43, journeys 0 -> 23). Total unchanged.
2026-11-12: dock scheduling added (src/dock/). Total 1310 -> 1315. This is new surface, not a regression: no existing module's count moved. Of the 14 tenant operations the module performs, 9 are contextualised because every write (create, reschedule, transition) runs inside withTenant(), which sets app.company_id so row-level security backs the WHERE clause rather than relying on it alone. The 5 that remain bare are reads: listing appointments, fetching one by id, computing a dock's free windows, checking for future bookings before deactivation, and resolving the warehouse. Each filters on companyId explicitly. They are bare because withTenant() is a transaction, costing a set_config round trip per call, and these are hot read paths. Two of them (getAppointment, availability) are also the guard in front of the writes, so an unscoped read there would 404 rather than leak.
